fact.text: Today is US Thanksgiving, yet roast turkey probably only became tied to the holiday around 1800.

lithuania.headline: EK kol kas netaikys Lietuvai perviršinio deficito procedūros
lithuania.summary: Europos Komisija prognozuoja, kad Lietuvos deficitas šiemet sieks 3,5 %, 2027 m. – 4,3 %, o 2028 m. – 5,1 % BVP, tačiau procedūros nepradės, nes 3 % ribos viršijimą lemia gynybos išlaidos; padėtį ji iš naujo vertins pavasarį. Komisija ragina drausminti 2027 m. biudžetą, o tam gali tekti mažinti paramą šeimoms ar įvesti naują mokestį.
lithuania.context: Nuo 2022 m., Rusijai užpuolus Ukrainą, Lietuva sparčiai didina gynybos išlaidas, todėl auga biudžeto deficitas. 2027 m. biudžeto projektas numato 3,8 % BVP deficitą ir 48,2 % skolą; praėjusią savaitę Seimas po pirmojo svarstymo grąžino jį Vyriausybei tobulinti, o koalicijoje kilo nesutarimų.

lithuania.headline: Sulaikyti penki įtariami dirbę Rusijos valstybinei žiniasklaidai
lithuania.summary: Prokuratūra sulaikė Kazimierą Juraitį, Vaidą Juozapaitytę, Dmitrijų Glazkovą, Lauryną Ragelskį ir Mindaugą Ramošką, įtariamus nuo 2024 m. rudens už atlygį rinkus informaciją ir skleidus Kremliaus naratyvus Rusijos valstybinei televizijai ir radijui. Atlikta daugiau nei 10 kratų, tyrimas susijęs su įstaiga „Tėvynės konduktoriai“.
lithuania.context: „Tėvynės konduktoriai“ užvertė valstybės institucijas šimtais užklausų jautriais klausimais; K. Juraitis jau teisiamas dėl padėjimo kitai valstybei veikti prieš Lietuvą, o L. Ragelskis anksčiau nuteistas už kurstymą.

lithuania.headline: Premjeras reikalauja tirti pasieniečius dėl kontrabandos
lithuania.summary: Mindaugas Sinkevičius pareikalavo nepriklausomo tyrimo dėl galimo pasieniečių dalyvavimo cigarečių kontrabandoje, o Vyriausybė naujuoju VSAT vadu patvirtino Donatą Škarnulį, žadantį kaltinimus ištirti. Šiemet dėl korupcinių veikų įtarimai pateikti 14 pasieniečių.
lithuania.context: Lazdijų rajono politikė Vilma Danauskienė paskelbė, kad VSAT naujokai jai pasakojo apie Imuniteto valdybos pareigūnų siūlymus ignoruoti cigarečių kontrabandą.

world.headline: Fuel tanker crash sparks fire killing 31 in Cairo
world.summary: A fuel tanker overturned and caught fire on Cairo's ring road in the Warraq area, killing at least 31 people, injuring 21 and burning more than two dozen vehicles; state media say a fallen high-voltage cable made the driver lose control, and the toll may rise.
world.why: Covered by 6 outlets, top of Google News World
world.context: Egypt has a poor road safety record: nearly 6,000 people died on its roads last year.

world.headline: US proposes new tariffs on China, EU and 12 others
world.summary: The US proposed tariffs of 20–40% on 14 trading partners, with China facing the highest rate; they need a hearing on 25 January and are unlikely to apply before February or March. Brazil called them 'unacceptable' and threatened retaliation, while China called them 'political manipulation'.
world.why: Covered by 8 outlets, front page of Google News
world.context: Trump imposed sweeping 'Liberation Day' tariffs in April 2025 using emergency powers, but the US Supreme Court ruled them illegal. In March the White House began investigating other countries' trade practices, and the new levies rely on the trade representative's authority instead.

world.headline: UK and EU publish post-Brexit reset treaties
world.summary: The UK publishes treaties on food trade and emissions trading agreed with the EU last week, plus a bill to enact them; a 10-year termination clause means a side that quits would pay to rebuild border-check infrastructure. The government forecasts a 16% boost to farm exports.
world.context: Britain left the EU in January 2020 after the 2016 referendum, and new checks hit trade. The two sides later agreed to 'reset' relations, and the deal agreed last week covers food exports, emissions trading and a youth scheme.

world.headline: Judges recommend dropping key Netanyahu charges
world.summary: Jerusalem judges told the attorney general there is little chance of convicting Benjamin Netanyahu in the bribery case over favours for positive media coverage, doubted a second case and suggested a plea deal in the third; the caretaker PM says the trial must end 'immediately'.
world.context: Netanyahu was charged in 2019 with bribery, fraud and breach of trust in three cases, and in 2020 became Israel's first sitting PM to stand trial. Hearings were slowed by the Gaza war; he denies wrongdoing and calls it a witch-hunt.

interesting.headline: SpaceX cleared to launch a million data-centre satellites
interesting.summary: The FCC approved SpaceX's Starmind plan for up to 1 million solar-powered AI data-centre satellites, despite objections from Amazon and astronomers; deployment must start by 2033, with the first satellite planned next year.
interesting.context: SpaceX already runs Starlink, with more than 10,000 internet satellites in orbit.

interesting.headline: Duran Duran guitarist Andy Taylor dies at 65
interesting.summary: Andy Taylor, who co-wrote Duran Duran hits such as Rio, Girls on Film and Save a Prayer, died at home on 23 November after a long fight with prostate cancer.
interesting.context: Duran Duran were one of the biggest pop acts of the 1980s.

interesting.headline: DART impact left a stadium-sized crater on asteroid
interesting.summary: First images from Europe's Hera probe show NASA's 2022 DART crash carved a crater almost as large as the 151-metre asteroid Dimorphos, which is now tumbling chaotically.
interesting.context: DART was a planetary defence test; the crash shortened Dimorphos's orbit around a larger asteroid by about 33 minutes.

interesting.headline: EA brings back John Motson with AI in FC 27
interesting.summary: EA Sports FC 27 adds the voice of commentator John Motson, who died in 2023, built from old recordings and generative AI with his family's paid consent; it goes live today.
interesting.context: Motson was the series' first commentator, from FIFA 96 to FIFA 2005.

ongoing.title: Russia-Ukraine war
ongoing.update: Russian ballistic missiles hit a shopping centre in Kyiv, injuring seven, after Ukraine said it damaged three MiG-31s and two Su-34s at Savasleyka airfield; Trump and NATO's Rutte urged Russia not to widen the war.
ongoing.context: Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022 after annexing Crimea in 2014. Kyiv repelled the push on the capital, then fighting settled into a long war of attrition in the east, with both sides increasingly striking deep behind the lines with drones and missiles.

ongoing.title: Nvidia CEO's affair with alleged Chinese spy
ongoing.update: Hegseth and Pentagon officials floated using a wartime law to reappoint Jensen Huang, and S&P said it may cut Nvidia's credit rating from AA to AA- over governance and 'key man' risks.
ongoing.context: This month Nvidia's founder Jensen Huang was pushed out after his affair with Alice Huang, an executive with alleged ties to Chinese intelligence, came to light. Within two weeks he returned as CEO with White House backing, and investigators are now asking what Nvidia knew about chips diverted via Megaspeed.

ongoing.title: Saudi Arabia-Houthi fighting
ongoing.update: Houthi fighters are encircling Aden, the government's temporary capital, about 80 km to its north, while a blast hit Sanaa after air strikes and missiles were intercepted over Riyadh.
ongoing.context: Yemen's Houthis seized Sanaa in 2014, and a Saudi-led coalition intervened in 2015 to back the government, which moved to Aden. In September the Houthis swept aside government forces, and this autumn they have struck Riyadh while the coalition hit Houthi ports.

ongoing.title: Cyber-attacks on European refrigeration systems
ongoing.update: French intelligence blamed an Iranian Revolutionary Guards hacking unit, Shahid Kaveh (CyberAv3ngers), for heating freezers in hundreds of French supermarkets; similar attacks hit 10 other countries this month.
ongoing.context: In October hackers cranked up temperatures in refrigeration systems at hundreds of French supermarkets, destroying millions of euros of food, and attacks spread to Sweden and elsewhere in November.
